VerifiedYouTubeProtocol.api_version: YouTube Data API v3; fetched method references report last updated 2026-10-15

scope.finding: One documented write-capable scope suffices for this insert/read/update integration; youtube.upload alone is NOT an accepted videos.update scope. Do not add youtube.readonly merely because read-back is required. Check granted scope, not just requested scope.

oauth.authorize: GET https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with client_id, exact registered redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, unpredictable state, access_type=offline; prompt=consent is available for reconsent; include_granted_scopes=true is optional.
oauth.exchange: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token; application/x-www-form-urlencoded: client_id, client_secret for confidential web client, code, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code, code_verifier when PKCE is used.
oauth.pkce: Per-request 43–128 character high-entropy unreserved ASCII code_verifier; code_challenge=base64url-without-padding(SHA256(ASCII(verifier))), code_challenge_method=S256. Official Node sample explicitly uses OAuth2Client(keys.web), generateCodeVerifierAsync(), generateAuthUrl({code_challenge_method:'S256',code_challenge}), getToken({code,codeVerifier}). The web-server REST table itself does not list PKCE; support is separately evidenced by Google's Node sample, not inferred from desktop-only guidance.
oauth.tokens: Successful token response: access_token, expires_in (seconds), token_type=Bearer, granted scope (space-delimited), optionally refresh_token; refresh_token_expires_in is documented for time-based access. Securely retain the prior refresh token if a later response omits one; do not assume every exchange returns a refresh token.
oauth.refresh: POST same token endpoint, form client_id, client_secret, grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token. Store new access token and expiry. invalid_grant/revocation requires reauthorization, not credential/account fallback.
oauth.testing: External OAuth consent screen + Testing gives seven-day refresh tokens unless ONLY identity/profile scopes are requested. YouTube scopes do not qualify for that exception. Production status does not guarantee perpetual validity.
oauth.version_note: Cloud's OAuth2Client reference currently labels its latest page 9.0.0; use the official sample as API evidence, not as proof of the repo's installed dependency version.

strict_callback.verified_fact: SameSite=Strict cookies are absent on the initial cross-site navigation back from Google; a callback cannot depend on the ordinary Strict session cookie being present.
strict_callback.recommendation: [INFERENCE/design] Preserve the main Strict cookie. At authenticated initiation, persist a short-lived state record bound to initiating owner/session, intended channel, exact redirect URI and PKCE verifier; set a separate unpredictable host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Lax correlation cookie, Secure on HTTPS. Permit only the dedicated GET callback through ordinary session-cookie middleware. Require BOTH state and the matching correlation cookie; verify initiating server-side session is still valid, expiry and exact callback parameters. Atomically claim/consume the state before exchange, including validated denial/error responses; reject replay, missing/mismatched binding and expired state without exchange. Clear the correlation cookie, use no-store/no-referrer and redirect to a clean URL. State lookup alone, a signed state alone, or PKCE alone must not authorize connecting credentials to an arbitrary app owner.
strict_callback.freshness: The Google web.dev SameSite article is dated 2019-05-07: baseline browser semantics, not new guidance or a verified project/browser test.

resumable.initiate: POST https://www.googleapis.com/upload/youtube/v3/videos?uploadType=resumable&part=snippet,status ; Authorization: Bearer TOKEN; Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8; X-Upload-Content-Length: N; X-Upload-Content-Type: video/mp4. Body includes approved snippet and explicit private/audience/disclosure status.
resumable.session: Documented successful initiation is HTTP 200 with Location. Persist the exact session URL before transmitting media. Official example origin/path is https://www.googleapis.com/upload/youtube/v3/videos with uploadType=resumable and upload_id; do not construct upload_id yourself.
resumable.transfer: PUT binary bytes to the saved Location. Completion is HTTP 201 with a video resource; persist its id immediately.
resumable.query: After interrupted/uncertain transfer, PUT saved Location with Authorization, Content-Length: 0, Content-Range: bytes */N. Completed session returns the original completion response. Incomplete returns 308 Resume Incomplete; Range: bytes=0-LAST means next byte LAST+1. Missing Range means zero bytes received. Honor Retry-After if supplied; 308 here is protocol progress, not a reason to follow a redirect.
resumable.resume: PUT same session with Content-Range: bytes FIRST-LAST/N and precisely the missing contiguous bytes. Query server state rather than assume previously sent bytes arrived. Guide recommends exponential backoff for 500/502/503/504.
resumable.origin_guard: [INFERENCE/security] Require exact trusted HTTPS origin/path, no URL userinfo, and no redirects to untrusted origins before attaching bearer tokens. Documentation supplies an example, not an exhaustive promise that every future session host is identical; unexpected hosts must block pending review rather than widen to arbitrary googleapis.com suffixes.

publication.bind_channel: GET https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/channels?part=id,snippet&mine=true ; match the authorized returned channel against the intended channel. No first-item/account fallback; onBehalfOfContentOwnerChannel is CMS-partner-only, not general channel selection.
publication.private_insert: Explicit status: {privacyStatus:'private', selfDeclaredMadeForKids: APPROVED_BOOLEAN, containsSyntheticMedia: APPROVED_BOOLEAN}; no publishAt.
publication.read_back: GET https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos?part=snippet,status,processingDetails&id=REMOTE_ID with owner OAuth. Require the exact item.id, snippet.channelId, approved snippet metadata, status.privacyStatus, status.selfDeclaredMadeForKids and status.containsSyntheticMedia. Missing disclosure/audience evidence is unknown, not false. selfDeclaredMadeForKids and processingDetails are owner-authorized fields.
publication.processing: processingDetails.processingStatus values: processing, succeeded, failed, terminated. Only succeeded is positive processing evidence; terminated means information unavailable, not success. status.uploadStatus values: deleted, failed, processed, rejected, uploaded; inspect failureReason/rejectionReason where applicable.
publication.public_update: PUT https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos?part=status ; body includes SAME id and complete intended mutable status: public visibility, approved selfDeclaredMadeForKids/containsSyntheticMedia and preserved license/embeddable/publicStatsViewable. Do not include snippet unless intentionally replacing it; snippet updates require title and categoryId.
publication.replacement_detail: Current update docs explicitly say mutable properties in supplied parts are replaced/deleted when omitted, BUT selfDeclaredMadeForKids and containsSyntheticMedia are specifically exempt and only update when explicitly set. Still resend both approved values to satisfy the publication contract. Never round-trip read-only uploadStatus/madeForKids as writable fields.
publication.completion: Revalidate manifest immediately before update; then owner-read-back same ID/channel, public visibility, metadata, audience/disclosure and processing. A transfer/update response alone does not prove contract completion.

uncertain_recovery.known_session: Query/resume that same persisted upload session; completed query recovers video.id. Never initiate another insert merely because media PUT timed out.
uncertain_recovery.known_video: Read back that same video ID after uncertain public update. Confirmed public+matching fields can finish; confirmed private remains blocked/recoverable under approved manifest; unavailable read-back remains UNKNOWN. Do not report confidently private/public from a transport error.
uncertain_recovery.lost_identity: [INFERENCE/contract] Persist intent before initiating and session before bytes. If initiation response/persistence is ambiguous, session disappears, or a completion may have happened but both session and video identity are unrecoverable, block for reconciliation. YouTube insert docs do not document a client Idempotency-Key or a deterministic local-intent-to-video lookup. Filename/title matching is not proof of identity.
uncertain_recovery.expired_session: Guide says expired session gives 404 and generally instructs starting over; that generic instruction does NOT justify a duplicate insert when this contract's earlier completion is uncertain. Preserve evidence and fail closed instead.

unknowns: No live credentials, account/channel availability, token behavior, uploads, processing, false-boolean omission behavior or publication were exercised; these are documentation facts and explicitly labeled adapter recommendations.
The session URL guide does not document an exhaustive host allowlist or exact expiration lifetime.
No provider-side idempotency key or exact recovery lookup from a local request ID is documented in the consulted insert/resumable references.
VerifiedYouTubeProtocol.coordination: Essential API, recovery, OAuth/PKCE, Strict-cookie and update-replacement facts sent to WorkspaceArchitecture in two IRC messages.
VerifiedYouTubeProtocol.read_only: No files created/modified, installs, accounts, credentials, provider actions, media transfers, formatters, linters or test suites.

VerifiedCommonsProtocol.title: Research: Commons source-media adapter under PW-03
VerifiedCommonsProtocol.answer: Use Commons Action API for discovery and original-file metadata, not as automatic rights clearance. Support only locally verified original formats, require human review of file-specific rights/attribution, and retain an original source-backed text-only title card when nothing is cleared. Essential facts and caveats were delivered to WorkspaceArchitecture by IRC.

search.response: With formatversion=2, query.pages[] contains pageid, ns:6, title, index (search rank), imagerepository and imageinfo[]. Continuation includes gsroffset; retain returned continuation parameters rather than manufacturing offsets. Without formatversion=2, documented pages is an object keyed by page ID.
search.filters: filetype:bitmap selects raster images; filetype:video selects videos. Neither restricts namespace by itself: retain gsrnamespace=6. filemime:"image/png" is exact; unquoted filemime accepts partial MIME-component matches. Search filtering is discovery, not validation.
search.limits: Search default 10, public maximum 500; current paraminfo exposes privileged highmax 5000, not a public guarantee. iilimit defaults to 1 and limits revisions PER FILE, not number of search results (public max500). extmetadata is explicitly expensive: request only a few files at a time. iiextmetadatafilter accepts pipe-separated keys, public maximum50. iiurlwidth requests scaled output and caps generated scaled images at50; omit scaling for original-only import.

imageinfo.fields: imageinfo[0].url is the original-file URL; descriptionurl is the Commons file-description page; descriptionshorturl is a short description-page URL. size is file bytes; width/height are pixels; pagecount applies when available. mime and mediatype describe the original. sha1 is the file SHA-1 (observed40-character hexadecimal); timestamp is upload-version time, NOT retrieval time. Missing/deleted/hidden fields are not usable-media proof.
imageinfo.actual_sample: The official CommonsMetadata example currently returns size:2897129, width:2000, height:2000, mime:"image/jpeg", mediatype:"BITMAP", sha1:"b72cae08ddb2c4a4d06d91d052cf0b78ed1ab74c", and original URL on https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cc/Common_Kingfisher_Alcedo_atthis.jpg with tracking query parameters.
imageinfo.extmetadata_shape: extmetadata is keyed by field name; each field is an object with value, source and optional hidden. Observed Artist.value and Credit.value contain HTML; AttributionRequired.value is the STRING "true"; Copyrighted.value is the STRING "True". Do not apply JavaScript truthiness to booleanish strings. Metadata values are not uniformly strings (the parser version value was numeric).

exact_keys.Artist: Author(s), potentially complex HTML; uploader is not necessarily creator.
exact_keys.Attribution: Custom attribution replacing Artist + Credit when supplied.
exact_keys.AttributionRequired: Booleanish legal attribution requirement; observed string, not native boolean.
exact_keys.Copyrighted: True/False classification; observed string with capital T.
exact_keys.Permission: May contain license templates, attribution instructions, permission identifiers and large HTML blocks.
exact_keys.Restrictions: Non-copyright restriction keywords (e.g. trademark/personality rights). Docs describe an array of keywords, but the live example exposes an object whose value is an empty string. Preserve raw representation; empty/missing is not evidence that no restrictions apply.
exact_keys.NonFree: Booleanish non-free marker documented chiefly for non-Commons files; absence is not positive clearance.
exact_keys.DeletionReason: Deletion consideration/reason signal; block or escalate for review.
exact_keys.License: Internal best guess; explicitly less reliable than LicenseShortName.

rights.caveats: CommonsMetadata extracts templates/categories and returns display-oriented HTML. LicenseShortName/LicenseUrl/UsageTerms/Copyrighted are explicitly unreliable for multi-licensed files. Preserve raw metadata evidence separately from safe plain-text/UI rendering; never execute returned HTML. Human review must resolve the chosen license, required credit/link/change notice, adaptation/ShareAlike obligations and non-copyright restrictions. Commons explicitly provides no copyright-status warranty.

download_formats.hosts: Confirmed original-download host: upload.wikimedia.org under /wikipedia/commons/. Description/redirect host: commons.wikimedia.org. Technical guidance also documents Special:FilePath / Special:Redirect/file (omitting width for full resolution). Do not promote thumb.wikimedia.org or /thumb/ preview URLs to original imports. Recommendation: accept only API-returned HTTPS originals on the exact supported host/path; validate redirects independently, not broad *.wikimedia.org or arbitrary Credit links.
download_formats.video: Commons documents WebM (.webm, VP8/VP9/AV1) and Ogg Theora (.ogv). Commons:File_types additionally mentions MPEG-1/2 .mpg/.mpeg, while the allowable-file-types policy omits them: do not promise these without resolving the discrepancy and verifying local support. MP4 ORIGINAL availability is UNVERIFIED/not listed in the reviewed allowed-original formats; do not infer it from player playback, transcodes or an app's MP4 decoder. Never invent an MP4 download by changing an original URL suffix.
download_formats.raster: Commons documents JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIFF and WebP raster formats, plus XCF; SVG is vector, not raster. Recommendation: start only with the intersection of these originals and the application's actually validated local decoders. JPEG/PNG are the smallest still-image support scope; adding other raster formats needs explicit local probe/decode coverage. Browser thumbnail compatibility is not original-format compatibility.

minimal_truthful_support.recommendation: Discover candidate originals; show their Commons description and raw rights evidence for explicit user review. Import only supported original bytes through a bounded, validated download path. Locally hash and probe/decode those bytes before treating them as renderable uploads; retain Commons SHA-1 as upstream evidence and local content hash separately. Version the source page/original URL, chosen license/evidence, attribution, retrieval time, local hash and video trim range. This is an implementation recommendation derived from canonical PW-03, not a claim of implemented or runtime-verified behavior.
minimal_truthful_support.fallback: If there is no cleared, supported footage or still, retain the story and use an original source-backed text-only title card. No uploaded image or fabricated image-license record is needed. Article/RSS/og:image thumbnails do not inherit clearance from being public. Generated illustration is not evidence of the reported event and the fallback authorizes no paid generation.
minimal_truthful_support.scope: No generic KOGL API, third-party media source support, accounts, credentials, provider changes, media downloads, file writes, implementation or tests were performed. Only official documentation/public JSON metadata were read.

VerifiedCommonsProtocol.version_notes: Facts checked2026-10-25. Commons generated API identified MediaWiki1.47.0-wmf.24; generic MediaWiki docs identified1.48.0-wmf.1, so Commons paraminfo was used for deployed limits. CommonsMetadata and search guidance were updated October2026. Technical reuse guidance was last edited2024-10-26 and is baseline guidance, not proof of current host completeness. Local decoder support, actual source import, file-specific legal clearance and MP4-original support remain explicitly unverified.

self_assessment.accuracy: 4/5: exact fields and sample responses checked; format-policy discrepancy and MP4 uncertainty retained rather than guessed.
self_assessment.completeness: 4/5: requested search/metadata/rights/hosts/formats/fallback covered; local codecs intentionally not exercised under read-only scope.
self_assessment.clarity: 4/5: facts, caveats and implementation recommendations separated; compactness limited by exact-field coverage.
self_assessment.actionability: 4/5: explicit query and minimal support contract supplied; actual importer still requires local verification outside this assignment.
self_assessment.conciseness: 4/5: grouped field definitions avoid a report file; full response is necessarily longer than the IRC handoff.
self_assessment.improvement: Before implementation sign-off, verify each advertised local decoder and resolve the documented MPEG policy discrepancy; do not expand support based on this research alone.

user_agent_policy.observed: Wikimedia requires a descriptive application/version User-Agent with operator contact URL/email for all metadata and original-media requests; generic/empty agents may be blocked with403. Do not spoof browser UA.
user_agent_policy.implementation: Configurable MEDIA_USER_AGENT on both api.php and upload.wikimedia.org fetches; explicit provider_blocked/provider_rate_limited results for403/429 with parsed Retry-After, never silently treat provider failure as no results or trigger fallback.
